summary_text: In May 2026, ten independent orders were placed across weekdays and weekends, with activity concentrated in the morning and afternoon dayparts. The basket profile is defined by a high frequency of fresh produce (Vegetables, Fruits) and dairy staples (Milk, Curd Yogurt), often combined with baby care items (Baby Cereal, Diaper) and pantry staples (Savouries, Aerated Drinks). While Vegetables appear in every order, no single category combination or daypart behavior recurs with sufficient frequency to establish a stable, high-confidence routine within this month alone. Occasional health-related purchases (Allopathy, Cough Remedy) and household cleaning items appear sporadically. Overall confidence is low due to the lack of repeated patterns across independent dates.

trend_claims.claim_text: Vegetables appear in every order across the month, indicating a consistent need for fresh produce, though no specific vegetable type or brand preference is established.

Baby care items (Baby Cereal, Diaper) and dairy staples (Milk, Curd Yogurt) frequently co-occur with fresh produce, suggesting a recurring household provisioning need for infant care and meal ingredients.
Health-related purchases (Allopathy, Cough Remedy) appear on separate dates (2026-05-14, 2026-05-22) but do not form a stable routine within this month.

shopping_need_text: Household provisioning for fresh produce, dairy, and infant care, with occasional health and household cleaning needs.
uncertainty_text: This analysis is based on ten independent orders across May 2026. While certain categories (Vegetables, Milk, Baby Cereal) appear frequently, no single combination or daypart behavior repeats with sufficient consistency to define a high-confidence stable routine. Confidence is medium for category pairs appearing on 2+ dates and low for sporadic health/cleaning items.
